claim_under_attack.claim_text: The field named `expected_calibration_error`, reported observationally at Phase-0 against a 0.10 ceiling that 'Phase-1 lock will gate at threshold with an independently double-labeled expert reference', is genuine Expected Calibration Error as defined in the calibration literature.
claim_under_attack.refutation_criterion: A refutation occurs if independently recomputing genuine binned ECE (Naeini et al. 2015 AAAI; Guo et al. 2017 PMLR 70) from the SAME fitted probabilities and true labels that produced the reported value yields a result differing from the reported value by more than 2x, robustly across multiple binning schemes (equal-width and equal-frequency, M ranging 2-20) -- i.e. the discrepancy is not an artifact of one arbitrary bin choice.
claim_under_attack.reported_note: Reported observationally at Phase-0. Phase-1 lock at config/benchmark-locks/amphora-molecule-role-ranker.v1.json will gate at threshold with an independently double-labeled expert reference.

does_not_close: EVALUATION_SIGNATURE_ABSENT (trust-anchored phase0-evaluator key absent from KPI file itself)
PHASE_1_INDEPENDENT_EVALUATION (needs an independently double-labeled expert reference per the KPI's own stated Phase-1 plan)
role_rule_correctness (out of scope; not touched by this audit)

genuine_ece_recomputation.robustness_note: Genuine ECE is essentially INVARIANT to bin count/scheme here (range ratio 1.833x across 13 distinct binning choices) because the fitted probabilities cluster tightly into two well-separated, well-populated groups (12 hardener records at p in [0.018,0.082], 12 resin records at p in [0.939,0.992]), so the discrepancy below is not a bin-edge artifact.

harness_source_citations.field_assignment_text: let expected_calibration_error = calibration_error_sum / resin_hardener_total.max(1) as f64;

interpretation: Independently re-deriving the 24 in-domain training records' fitted resin-probabilities from the shipped frozen model artifact (zero transcription of the reported number) and computing mean Brier score reproduces the shipped KPI's expected_calibration_error observed value (0.0019924703593823217) EXACTLY (match=True), proving the harness's `calibration_error_sum += brier; ... / resin_hardener_total` (role_ranker_phase0_kpi.rs L412) computes mean Brier score, not binned ECE. Computing genuine M-bin ECE (Guo et al. 2017) from the identical probabilities and labels gives 0.02242-0.041097 across 13 distinct binning schemes (equal-width M=2..20, equal-frequency M=2..12), a spread of only 1.833x -- essentially bin-choice-invariant because the fitted probabilities separate cleanly into two tight clusters. Genuine ECE is 11.3x the reported value (0.0224 vs 0.002), exceeding the pre-registered 2x refutation threshold. CLAIM_REFUTED: the field named `expected_calibration_error` in the flagship KPI is mechanically the mean Brier score, a related but numerically distinct statistic from Expected Calibration Error, and readers/gate-designers relying on the field name would materially underestimate the model's actual (still small, still reporting-only, still under-ceiling) miscalibration on its own training data. Scope: reporting-only field; no Phase-0 gate flips; role-classification-kpi.v1.json is left unmodified pending a properly-scoped repair (R-/V- item) to rename the field or compute genuine ECE alongside it.

method.step_1: Load shipped fixture reference/phase0-role-known-answer.v1.json and its frozen fitted_model_artifact (coefficients + z-score standardization).
method.step_2: Independently port role_ranker_phase0_kpi.rs::fitted_resin_probability (the harness's own sigmoid-over-standardized-features formula) to Python, applied to the same 24 training records, from raw fixture facts only (no transcription of probabilities or the reported metric).
method.step_3: Compute mean Brier score from the independently-derived probabilities; confirm it reproduces the shipped KPI's published expected_calibration_error observed value byte-for-byte, validating the re-derivation is faithful and non-circular (proves what the harness ACTUALLY computes).
method.step_4: Compute genuine binned ECE (Guo et al. 2017 formula) and MCE from the SAME probabilities and true labels, across 7 equal-width and 6 equal-frequency binning schemes (M = 2..20), to rule out a bin-choice artifact.
method.step_5: Compare reported value against the full spread of genuine ECE values.

primary_references: Naeini, M.P.; Cooper, G.F.; Hauskrecht, M. (2015) 'Obtaining Well Calibrated Probabilities Using Bayesian Binning', AAAI 29(1):2901-2907.
Guo, C.; Pleiss, G.; Sun, Y.; Weinberger, K.Q. (2017) 'On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks', PMLR 70:1321-1330 (canonical M-bin ECE/MCE formula).
Brier, G.W. (1950) 'Verification of Forecasts Expressed in Terms of Probability', Monthly Weather Review 78(1):1-3. doi:10.1175/1520-0493(1950)078<0001:VOFEIT>2.0.CO;2

Murphy, A.H. (1973) 'A New Vector Partition of the Probability Score', J. Appl. Meteorol. 12(4):595-600 (Brier decomposition: reliability - resolution + uncertainty; reliability term is NOT numerically equal to ECE).
purpose: ROTATION-mode metric-definition-integrity audit of the flagship KPI's expected_calibration_error field: verify by independent re-derivation whether the reported statistic is genuine binned Expected Calibration Error (ECE) or a differently-named statistic (mean Brier score).

reproduction.interpretation: Exact match confirms the field the harness names `expected_calibration_error` is, mechanically, the mean squared error of the fitted probabilities against the true 0/1 labels (Brier score), NOT a binned reliability statistic.

risk_note: The reported_ceiling comparison (0.10, 'Phase-1 lock will gate at threshold') is currently being read against the WRONG statistic: the true in-sample calibration picture on this model's own training data is genuine ECE ~0.0224 (~22.4% of the stated 0.10 ceiling), not the reported Brier-score value ~0.002 (~2.0% of ceiling). This changes the safety-margin narrative a reader would take from the Phase-0 observational trend by roughly 11.3x, even though this metric is explicitly 'reporting_only' at Phase-0 and gates nothing today.

scope_boundary.NOT_A_CORRECTNESS_CLAIM_ABOUT_THE_ROLE_R: This audit is about metric-definition integrity of one reporting-only field; it makes no claim about and does not touch structural_inference_agreement_rate=1.0, the deterministic role rule, or any prior SURVIVED/REFUTED verdict on role classification itself.
scope_boundary.NOT_A_GATING_FAILURE: The metric already carries passed_reporting_only=true and is explicitly not gated at Phase-0 ('Phase-1 lock will gate at threshold with an independently double-labeled expert reference'), so no Phase-0 pass/fail flips. The defect is that the number under that field is not what its name says it is, which matters for whoever designs the Phase-1 gate against this Phase-0 trend line.
scope_boundary.TARGET_UNCHANGED: role-classification-kpi.v1.json, role_ranker_phase0_kpi.rs and the fixture are left byte-intact; this is a new, separate audit artifact, not an edit.
